newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes higher as recovery firms.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes higher as recovery firms.

text.p: The Czech PX50 and RPIX indices consolidated their recovery on Friday with major issues rising strongly and turnover doubling to 1.5 billion crowns.
The PX50 rose 1.6 percent to 557.9 and the RPIX rose 2.5 percent to 1,134.

Despite an array of formidable gains from the major issues dealers said prices on the bourse probably overstated true market values in many cases and referred to over-the-counter (OTC) trading, which accounts for around 80 percent of total volume, as a better guide.
"Closing prices were lower on the OTC market. Real market prices are a bit lower," said Karel Ruzicka of ING Barings.

Ruzicka quoted power utility CEZ as one example. CEZ surged 34 crowns, 3.4 percent, to 1,039 on the bourse but closed at around 1,020 on the OTC market. A similar pricture emerged with many other shares, he said.

However, despite Ruzicka's note of caution, he conceded that that the rebound was real, albeit overstated, and said the situation in the Czech equity market had calmed down after the crisis at Agrobanka last week had dented confidence.
"I think the situation has stabilised," he said.
